subtype: Approach: planning fallacy about irregular expenses [Pitfall]
passage: Kunal from the accounts desk here. I sit near Rekha, and I'll describe what I saw this winter without claiming to know what went on inside. In January Rekha proudly showed me a monthly budget that looked perfect: rent, groceries, transport, savings. Then an insurance premium arrived, then festival gifts for relatives, then a laptop repair in the same quarter. None of them were in the sheet. Rekha went quiet at lunch and skipped the canteen for a few days. I saw the sheet again in March and the savings column had been used to cover the gap. Rekha said only, "These costs come every year, I just forgot them." I can't say how it felt, but it did not look easy.

qa.q: Which three expenses arrived in the same quarter and were not in the sheet?
qa.a: An insurance premium, festival gifts for relatives and a laptop repair arrived and were not in the sheet.

qa.q: What might Rekha have been feeling when saying the costs come every year?
qa.a: Rekha may have felt embarrassed or upset, since Rekha went quiet and said the costs were simply forgotten, though Kunal cannot be sure.

qa.q: What could Rekha add to the budget, and why?
qa.a: Rekha could list the yearly costs and set aside a small amount each month for them, because lumpy costs then stop breaking the plan.

qa.q: How might Kunal see Rekha's situation from the next desk?
qa.a: Kunal saw Rekha's quiet days and the used savings and feels concerned, but admits not knowing what Rekha felt inside.

grounding: A budget that covers monthly costs but leaves out annual items breaks when several such bills fall in one quarter.
